properties.title: Abstract Security — Activity Log export (one subscription)

steps.name: basics
steps.label: Basics
steps.description:
Streams **one** subscription's Azure Activity Log to an Abstract Event Hub.

This is a **subscription-scope** deployment — there is no resource group to pick, because a subscription diagnostic setting is not a resource-group resource. That is also why this form uses the Form view (`uiFormDefinition`) model rather than `createUiDefinition`: only Form view can bind a portal deployment to a subscription, management group or tenant scope.

**Onboarding a whole estate?** Use the governance pack instead — assign it once at a management group and every subscription, current and future, onboards itself. This template is for a single subscription or a quick proof.

options.text: Prerequisite: the Event Hub and its namespace-level Send authorization rule must already exist. Deploy the Event Hub source template first and take the abstractDiagnosticsAuthRuleId and eventHubNames outputs from it — this template never creates hubs.

location.label: Deployment metadata region
location.toolTip: Where the deployment record is stored. The Activity Log itself is not regional, so this does not affect collection.

elements.name: settingName
elements.label: Diagnostic setting name
elements.toolTip: Azure allows a maximum of five diagnostic settings per subscription. If the customer already streams to another SIEM, this is an ADDITIONAL setting and does not displace it — but the ceiling is real.

steps.name: hub
steps.label: Event Hub
steps.description: Where the Activity Log is delivered.

options.text: The region rule does NOT apply here. Azure Monitor requires an Event Hub to share a region with the monitored resource only when that resource is regional — a subscription is not. One hub therefore serves every subscription in the estate, wherever its resources live.

elements.name: eventHubAuthorizationRuleId
elements.label: Event Hubs authorization rule ID
elements.toolTip: Namespace-level rule with Send rights — the abstractDiagnosticsAuthRuleId output of the Event Hub source template. Send alone is sufficient when the hub already exists, despite Microsoft's docs listing Manage+Send+Listen; the wider rights only matter if Azure Monitor has to create the hub for you.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be a full namespace-level authorization rule resource ID ending in /authorizationrules/<rule>.

elements.name: eventHubName
elements.label: Event Hub name
elements.toolTip: Must already exist. The source template auto-names hubs <hubPrefix>-<environment>-<source>, so its defaults produce abs-prod-activity. Check the eventHubNames output rather than trusting this default — a name that does not exist fails silently.

constraints.validationMessage: 1-256 characters: letters, numbers, periods, hyphens, underscores.

steps.name: categories
steps.label: Categories
steps.description: Which Activity Log categories to stream.

elements.name: categories
elements.label: Activity Log categories
elements.toolTip: Abstract recommends all eight. Activity Log volume is modest and the pipeline filters downstream, so narrowing here only creates blind spots you cannot recover retroactively.

allowedValues.label: Security — Defender for Cloud alerts surfaced in Activity Log

options.text: Expect data within about 90 minutes of deployment. An empty hub in the first few minutes is normal, not a failure. If nothing arrives within 24 hours, disable and re-enable the setting before escalating.
